summary: Four procedures every host walks. Bodies are prose for judgement; the steps are verbs to RUN.

skills.description: Use when a kit verb stops at a DOOR (exit 3, 'this is a DOOR'): an approval only the host's owner may give. Shows what the door decides, runs the plan, and asks the owner -- never approves on their behalf.

Use when a rule of this repository should bind every agent and every commit: adds a numbered law and, where text can show the violation, a calibrated edit gate. Not for preferences or one-off instructions.

Use before changing anything in this repository, and while doing it: weighs the change (its work class, what it owes, who it affects, the lessons of where it touches), leaves exactly the records its class requires, and captures what is met on the way. Not for answering a question -- that changes nothing.
Use when this host should take a published adapter, bundle or policy (a new product, toolchain, doctrine or rule set): plans the take, then hands the approval to the owner.
